text: Conversely, the medial and lateral heads are more active during movements such as the triceps pushdown, in which the humerus is held at the sides (139). This renders the long head less active so that the other heads carry out a greater amount of work. The applied theory is somewhat supported by the findings of Stasinaki and colleagues (130), who compared triceps training at a long muscle length (overhead triceps extension) versus at a short muscle length (triceps pushdowns) in untrained subjects.
